name: Residential and Commercial Cleaning
purpose: AhernAI sales discovery and illustrative configuration guidance
summary: For residential or commercial cleaning businesses. Clarify services, inquiry handling, estimate scheduling and routine customer requests. A message-only need is a valid Level 1 fit. Ask one useful question at a time about the caller's actual workflow. Explain Level 1 when messages and FAQs fit; move directly to Level 2 when the caller needs routine work completed. Recommend the lowest suitable level as soon as the need is understood; no mandatory three-level tour. Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.
discovery_questions: Do you clean homes, commercial premises or both?
Are most inquiries recurring service, one-time cleaning, move-out work or something else?
What happens when someone calls while the crew is working?
Which questions about service area, scope or estimates come up repeatedly?
Do you want staff to call back, book an estimate visit or receive a qualified lead in your CRM?
Which complaints, access concerns or scheduling exceptions need a supervisor?

levels.name: Answering Service
use_cases: Answer approved FAQs about service areas and cleaning categories without inventing inclusions or prices.
Capture caller details, residential or commercial scope, general property size, desired timing and the reason for calling.
Send a new inquiry, schedule-change request or service concern as a summary to one agreed destination for staff follow-up.
levels.probe: Would an organized message with the property and cleaning needs let your team handle the next step?
fit_signals: Calls go unanswered while crews are working.
Staff want to review requests before quoting or scheduling.

levels.name: Receptionist
use_cases: Qualify property type, service area and approved service needs, and offer screened transfers when human review is required.
Book or change eligible estimate visits or cleaning appointments and update agreed customer records with the supporting automation included.
Route routine customer requests to the agreed office queue using approved rules, without promising staff availability or collecting sensitive access codes.
levels.probe: Which estimate or appointment requests can follow your normal office rules?
fit_signals: The caller needs routine receptionist work completed rather than only a message.
Approved business rules and verified systems support the agreed workflow.

levels.name: Manager
use_cases: Gather detailed missed-service, quality or damage concerns and the caller's requested resolution for a supervisor.
Explain approved cancellation or service policies and escalate disputed charges or exceptions without making a decision.

Support approved employee coordination, such as recording a shift callout or coverage request and routing it to the authorized supervisor. Employment, staffing approval, disciplinary, financial and policy-exception decisions remain human; do not request medical reasons or other sensitive employee details.
levels.probe: Only after the caller raises a management need: Which situations should the agent handle under approved rules, and which should reach you?
fit_signals: The caller asks for help with difficult or disgruntled callers and escalations.
The caller wants approved employee coordination or supervisory support.

scope_boundaries: Do not request door, gate or alarm codes, keys, payment-card details or other access credentials during discovery or example intake.
Do not give chemical-mixing instructions or hazardous cleanup advice. Use approved human escalation for hazards or work outside the business's confirmed scope.
Do not promise a fixed quote, crew availability, rescheduling, arrival time, damage responsibility or a re-clean without an approved policy and configured capability.

Human staff decide refunds, credits, discounts, liability and policy exceptions. Texting and additional transfer usage charges retain their separately disclosed terms; included receptionist automation is not a separate build fee.

Level 1 captures approved FAQs, caller details and a summary to one destination; it does not book, submit orders, update a CRM or make screened transfers. Level 2 covers agreed routine receptionist duties and supporting automation. Package fit is based on duties, not a one-calendar/one-CRM or two-integration quota. Scope is agreed before launch; this is not an unlimited software-development commitment.

Routine receptionist duties and the supporting automation are included in the agreed Level 2 scope, without an additional AhernAI automation or integration-build charge. Confirm software compatibility, access, allowed actions and failure handling during setup; an unverified connection is not an automatic surcharge.

Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.

Do not promise that a named app or POS is supported merely because the caller names it. Verify compatibility during setup and agree a workable destination or fallback; disclose any actual work outside the agreed duties before proceeding.
setup_requirements: Confirm residential/commercial focus, offered cleaning categories, service area, business hours and excluded work.
Supply approved FAQs, estimate rules, intake fields and the single summary destination.
Define appointments or CRM fields, qualification, transfer contacts and escalation fallbacks.
Provide cancellation, complaint and damage-reporting policies, plus a separate approved access-detail process.
Confirm compatibility; test inquiries, unavailable appointments and complaints before launch.
Agree the routine duties and supporting automation included in the package, approved actions, access permissions, successful completion signals and failure paths before launch.

adjacent_services.trigger: Callers cannot tell which cleaning services are offered.
adjacent_services.example: Explore service pages and an inquiry form with approved scope questions.

adjacent_services.trigger: The business needs broader back-office work beyond its agreed receptionist duties.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a separate project only for that broader need. Automation needed for agreed Level 2 receptionist work is already included; do not resell it as a Quickstart or add-on.

example_conversation.speaker: caller
example_conversation.text: We are a cleaning company and just need missed calls recorded.

example_conversation.speaker: agent
example_conversation.text: Level 1 could answer approved questions and send a clear callback summary. Would you want your office to handle all booking?

example_conversation.speaker: agent
example_conversation.text: Then Level 1 sounds like the right starting point. What details should each callback message include?
